topic: A9: Backend compare latency: where the 20-30 s goes and what a knowledge-base-first serve could skip
summary:
Answer: a cold text compare takes 22-30 s for three reasons. Each product's legs run one after another inside _fetch_product_data. The price race is slow. And nothing is reused at the pair level. On the app's explicit-pair path the parse and category steps cost about 0 s. The time goes to the per-product chain.

The chain is: unified Serper search (12 s bound), then the specs/reviews/image races (8 / 10 / 5 s, and none of them starts until the search returns), then Phase 2 (rating 4 s + smart fallback 5 s), then Tier 2 (4 s), then Tier 3 (3 s), one after another. The price race (15 s) runs alongside it. Worst case for the chain is about 34 s, against a 30 s cap.

Measured in the S78 log window:
- The price race missed 23 of 30; the image race hit its timeout 20 times; the unified search timed out 5 times.
- Serper shopping took 3.1-13.1 s (median about 8.3 s, n=13).
- Phase 1 ended with only 1.1-7.9 s left before the cap, so partials stop at stage=gather.
- After the pair, the tail (verdict, then moderation) takes about 6.1 s.

The prior digest's "Phase-1 worst case about 12+10 s" is correct but understated: it leaves out the serial Phase-2 and Tier-2/3 tail. The rest still holds at 95cf6f86; line numbers have moved by about 24.

Known pairs are not faster today. A cache-warm second run took 22.7-30.8 s. The reasons:
- There is no pair or verdict cache.
- The image and the rating have no cache at all.
- The gpt-4o verdict and moderation always run.
- Partials and searches that timed out cache nothing.

SSE: every data event (specs, prices, reviews, first_paint, scores) is yielded only after both products have finished the whole chain. Only status 10/20 arrive early. Build 3 does not use SSE at all: it makes one REST call with a 35 s timeout and shows a checklist timed on the client.

A knowledge-base-first serve for a known pair could skip:
- the unified search, and the specs and reviews LLM calls;
- smart fallback and Tier 2/3;
- the image, the rating and category resolution.

Some things must still run live: price freshness (serve the stored price with its age, refresh it in a bounded or background call), the deterministic scoring with personalization (milliseconds), and the verdict when the preferences or data hash change. Moderation is needed only for new text.

Proposed budget:
- Cold pair: about 16 s p50 (1 route + max(8 price, 6 search + 4 extract) + 5 verdict + 0.6).
- Known pair: about 1.5 s with a cached base verdict, about 6.5 s with a personalized one, 10 s at most with a live price refresh.

The three changes that would move p50 most: (1) a dark pair-level KB-first serve; (2) moving the Phase-2 and Tier fills into background KB enrichment, with ENABLE_TIER_FILL_RESIDUAL_GUARD as the interim step; (3) taking price freshness off the critical path, plus reserving the verdict tail.

findings.claim: The REST compare is one asyncio.wait_for(STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS) around _compare_from_text_impl; the code default is 25.0 and prod runs 30.0. The impl stamps self._compare_deadline (the deadline the Phase-2 and tier guards read) at entry.

The route does serial work before the compare: the paid-route auth guard, then get_user_preferences, then consume_comparison_credit (Supabase/Redis on the loop while ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is OFF). After the compare, persist, log_search and metering are fire_and_forget, so persistence is off the critical path unless ENABLE_COMPARISON_ID_ECHO is ON (it is dark).

findings.claim: On the app's explicit-pair path, parse and category cost about 0 s. Parse is skipped (no LLM), and the category is deterministic. The bounded A2b LLM call (4 s) runs only when the names are blind AND no chip is set. The q-form parse LLM runs only for typed 'A vs B' queries, and ENABLE_PARSE_PRESPLIT is dark.
evidence: C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s80-b2/app/services/structured_comparison_service.py:483-491 - A2b only when det=other and no chip

findings.claim: Within each product, specs, reviews and image are not parallel with the search. They are created only AFTER the unified Serper search returns. That search is bounded at 12 s (ENABLE_UNIFIED_SEARCH_BOUND ON in prod), and it is skipped only when BOTH the specs and the reviews L1 entries hit. The specs path is therefore up to 12 + 8 s, reviews up to 12 + 10 s and image up to 12 + 5 s. The price task starts before the search and runs concurrently under a 15 s cap.

findings.claim: After the Phase-1 gather, each product runs a SERIAL tail: a Phase-2 gather (rating 4 s cap plus smart fallback 5 s), then Tier 2 (4 s), then Tier 3 (gpt-4o, 3 s), awaited one after another. The worst-case product chain is about 12+10+5+4+3 = 34 s, more than the 30 s cap. The prior digest's 'Phase-1 worst case about 12+10 s' is correct but omits this tail.

Measured production leg times from the S78 07:00 window (30 products):
- 23 price-race timeouts, 20 image-race timeouts, 6 reviews, 5 specs and 5 unified-search timeouts.
- Phase 2 was skipped 20 times, with 1.1-7.9 s left. Phase 1 therefore consumed about 22-29 s of the 30 s cap.
- Serper shopping took 3,145-13,143 ms (median about 8.3 s, n=13).
- Tier 2 timed out 6 of 6.
- The cap hit 8 times.

findings.claim: Once the pair returns, the tail is: fairness and guards (CPU), awaiting the profile task, deterministic scoring (ms), the gpt-4o verdict, self-critique (OFF), trust validation and response build (sub-second), then L3 moderation. The verdict-to-moderation tail measured 6.1 s; TAIL_RESERVE_SECONDS defaults to 6.5 s on that basis.

Stage classification:
- Pure cache, DB or CPU: specs L1/L2, reviews L1/L2, price L1/L2/negcache, prefs/credit/profile, drug DB, rating Tier 1 from the in-request shopping cache, fairness, scoring and build.
- Network, not LLM: the unified search, Serper shopping plus the Tier-1.5 fan-out, Serper Images, the US-shopping rating fallback, and the smart-fallback and Tier-2 searches.
- LLM: q-form parse, A2b category, specs and reviews extraction, smart-fallback, Tier-2 mini per field, Tier-3 gpt-4o, price Tier 2/3 estimate, image Tier-3 GPT, the verdict, critique (OFF), and moderation.

findings.claim:
Repeat compares are not faster today. The warm-up script runs without nocache, and its cache-warm second run took 22.7-30.8 s against 27.7-32.5 s on the first. The reasons:
- There is no pair-level result or verdict cache (text_routes reads no compare cache).
- image_service has no cache.
- The rating has no persistence.
- The verdict and moderation always run.
- Partials write no cache, and specs or reviews extracted after a unified-search timeout are never cached (FY19).
evidence: C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s80-b2/scripts/review_warmup.py:4 - 'no nocache, so the answers are cached'

findings.claim:
SSE order on /text/compare/stream:
1. status 10 ('Parsing query').
2. status 20.
3. The Phase-1 gather of both products, bounded by a 30 s wait_for.
4. specs, prices, status 50, reviews, first_paint, scores, status 80, verdict.
5. settle_complete, then complete.
Every data event is emitted only after BOTH products finish the whole per-product chain, so specs, prices and reviews arrive together at about 22-29 s. The tail after the gather is unbounded unless ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE is set (dark).
evidence: C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s80-b2/app/services/structured_comparison_service.py:5287,5322,5534 - tail wait_for only under the flag

findings.claim: Build 3 renders nothing progressive from the server. SSE is off (ENABLE_EXPO_FETCH_SSE_DEFAULT=false), so the text path is a single REST call with a 35 s timeout. The loader is a checklist timed on the client, landing stages at 1.2 / 4.2 / 12 / 19.5 / 26 s. The camera path has no stream route at all. Making it progressive needs a client OTA, which is blocked until after approval.

A partial at stage=gather loses the image and the reviews. The early buffer stashes only specs and price through done-callbacks; the image and reviews tasks sit inside the same gather and are cancelled with it.

evidence: C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s80-b2/CLAUDE.md:337 area (Cost budget + caching) - L2 specs 30 d, reviews 14 d

findings.claim: Some steps must stay live on a known pair. Price freshness: L1 prices expire after 24 h, or 7 d for genuine BH prices; the L2 window is the same. Deterministic scoring with preferences, behaviour and cohort (ms, no LLM). The verdict when its inputs change: generate_comparison receives user_preferences, the scores summary, demographics, the comparison quality and output_lang, so a cached verdict is valid only for an identical input key. The usage gate and auth also stay live.

The two dark S78 levers address the serial tail but remain unflipped. ENABLE_TIER_FILL_RESIDUAL_GUARD (Tier 2/3 skip below 4/3 s plus a 6.5 s reserve) and ENABLE_SERPER_KEY_STATE_MEMO were merged in S79 as #355/#356, default OFF and unset in prod. PHASE2_MIN_RESIDUAL_SECONDS=12 is live. Plan fix #6 (reserve the verdict tail at the pair barrier) was never built.

Search and image latency is driven by Serper. Sampled Serper spans: ok p50 3.5 s / p95 12.4 s, failures p50 5.9 s / p95 16.9 s, about 45% failed. The Serper Images HTTP timeout (15 s, or 10 s + 8 s) is longer than the 5 s image cap, so a slow Tier 1 consumes the whole image budget and Tier 3 never runs.

findings.claim:
The p50 figures differ by source:
- Organic search_logs series: p50 22.0 s (CLAUDE.md W3-2 row and the full-review note).
- Sampled backend text compares: 30.5-34.8 s.
- Client text wall: median 32.7 s (n=7).
The 22 s p50 includes cache-warm and fast pairs, while the Sentry samples are cold pairs at the cap.

findings.claim: Anthropic latency is not measured anywhere in the repo or the prior runs: Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 time to first token and total time, and the round trips of the server-side web_search tool. Putting web_search on the critical path in place of the unified Serper search could add, rather than save, seconds. It should be measured off-clock first.

recommendations: Build a pair-level KB-first serve behind a new dark flag (for example ENABLE_KB_FIRST_SERVE; default OFF, read per call, byte-identical when OFF). Read both products' KB rows (specs, reviews, image_url, rating, category, price with fetched_at) in one round trip before _fetch_product_data, and return early from the per-product chain on a full hit. This is the only lever that turns today's 22.7-30.8 s warm runs into about 1.5-7 s.

Move smart fallback, Tier 2 and Tier 3 off the request path into a background KB-enrichment job that writes the KB and L1/L2. Until then, flip the merged ENABLE_TIER_FILL_RESIDUAL_GUARD after its canary. This removes up to 12 s of serial tail per product (scs:6247-6339), and Tier 2 was 6/6 timeouts anyway.

Take price freshness off the critical path: serve the KB price with its age, and refresh with stale-while-revalidate. A live refresh should be one bounded fetch per known merchant PDP URL from the merchant registry, about 4-5 s, observing robots fail-closed and stopping at Cloudflare. Serper shopping alone has a median of about 8.3 s and the 15 s race missed 23/30.

Cache the base (unpersonalized) verdict per (pair identity, data hash, lang, model, prompt version), with its moderation result. Regenerate it only when preferences, cohort or the data hash change; keep deterministic scoring live. This saves the 6.1 s verdict-plus-moderation tail on repeat views.

Build S78 fix #6 (reserve the verdict tail at the pair barrier) behind a dark flag, so a cold compare always reaches the verdict instead of a stage=gather partial without pros. The Phase-1 residual was 1.1-7.9 s in S78.

Start the image race before the unified search, or read the image from the KB. Add a done-callback early stash (R0-B7), so a gather partial keeps an image that had already resolved; the image race timed out 20 times in the S78 window.

Change the stream generator to emit specs and prices per product as each lands, not after both chains finish. This is backend-additive; build 3 ignores it because SSE is off, and the client half is an OTA after approval.
Do not raise STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS: the app aborts at 35 s. Do not flip ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE together with ENABLE_HONEST_PARTIAL_SCORING. Keep both rulings from the S78 hold list.

Measure Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and web_search latency off-clock, in the enrichment job, before any of them replaces Serper or gpt-4o on the request path. Budget each LLM leg at 4-5 s inside the existing per-race caps.

Before and after each change, read metadata.stage_timings_ms (DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS is ON in prod) and the B1 compare_ms buckets once ENABLE_RESULT_STATUS_METADATA flips. Note that partials carry no stage_timings_ms today, so the slowest compares are invisible to that field.
open_questions: What is the share of compares whose two products are both already in the L1/L2 specs and reviews caches? This sizes the KB-first win. It needs owner-run read-only SQL over product_specs and product_reviews against search_logs; no agent DB access.
Are partial (stage=gather) responses counted in the 22.0 s organic p50, and what is the p50 split by cold versus warm?
What are the Anthropic Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 time-to-first-token and total times for the verdict prompt size, and the web_search tool round-trip time? None is measured.
Is ENABLE_PARSE_PRESPLIT set on web? No ledger records it. It matters only for q-form queries.
Can the merchant registry hold enough fresh PDP URLs per fragrance product to replace Serper shopping discovery under the robots fail-closed ruling? Fragrancex already 403s Railway egress.
Which stage_timings keys does the partial builder omit? Adding timings to partials would make the cap-hitting compares measurable.
